_doc: Value engineering (Q6154): the wiring-method alternatives CADaddy weighs, as data. `methods`: the words a specification's wiring-methods table uses for each method. `code_sheet`: the words a code-analysis sheet labels its facts with. `areas`: how the model's rooms are classified (each alternative names the classes it is never used in). Each alternative swaps the designed method for another where the code allows it: the circuits it applies to (`circuit`, `areas`, `to`), the spec application words it must match (`application`, none of `application_not`), the construction types the code allows it in, the code's cites, its conditions, the places it is never used (`excluded_areas`, with why), the ampacity column its conductors are checked at, and the design intents it is weighed against. Tiers: allowed_now (the spec lists the alternative for the application and the code allows it), needs_rfi (the code allows it, the spec doesn't), not_proposed (it can't meet the design's likely intent), not_allowed (the code doesn't allow it here). The cites are NEC numbering (2017 through 2023 keep these numbers).

code_sheet.source: the code-analysis sheet's own labels (IBC chapters 3, 5, 6, 9; the codes in force)

unit.name: dwelling and guest units
unit.source: the router's area: a typical unit's circuits, or rooms named as units (conduitroute.json methods.unit_words)

common.name: common areas, concealed
common.source: the router's area: concealed in walls and ceilings outside the units

exposed.name: exposed (mechanical, electrical and service rooms)
exposed.source: the router's area: rooms named in conduitroute.json methods.exposed_rooms

suspended.name: above suspended (lay-in) ceilings
suspended.source: the RCP: the room's ceiling type is a suspended grid

plenum.name: air-handling (plenum) ceilings
plenum.source: a room or ceiling type named a plenum (NEC 300.22(C))

rated_corridor.name: fire-rated corridors
rated_corridor.source: a corridor (the spec's circulation or a room so named) where the code sheet or the wall types give rated assemblies

below_slab.name: below slabs-on-grade, in concrete and underground
below_slab.source: a run below the floor of the lowest level

ceiling_unknown.name: ceilings the documents don't type
ceiling_unknown.source: no RCP ceiling and no room finish over the run: whether it is a suspended ceiling's cavity is not documented
ceiling_unknown.confirm: the documents don't say whether the ceilings over these runs are gypsum or suspended: confirm none is a suspended ceiling's cavity (NEC 334.12(A)(2)) before choosing it

crew.source: company default: a crew of 4 electricians at 8 h a day (the job's own crew overrides: `crew_size`, `hours_per_day`)

ampacity.source: NEC Table 310.16 (75 °C and 90 °C insulation; 60 °C column), copper and aluminum
ampacity.next_size_up_source: NEC 240.4(B): the next standard size up (240.6(A)) protects a conductor whose ampacity doesn't match one, up to 800 A

bundling.source: NEC 334.80: more than two cables of two or more current-carrying conductors through one bored hole sealed with firestop or caulk, or in contact with thermal insulation, are adjusted by 310.15(C)(1) (the 90 °C rating may be derated, the result not above the 60 °C column)

firestop.source: IBC 714 / NEC 300.21: each penetration of a fire-rated assembly sealed with a system listed for what passes through it (a raceway's system is not a cable's)

intents.reason: specifier default: the specification's wiring-methods article lists conductors in raceway for this application as a master specification does, not for a reason the job states
intents.meets: the alternative is a method the code permits for the building's construction type; the conductors, protection and routing stay as designed

intents.reason: fire rating: the runs pass through fire-rated walls or floors
intents.meets: each rated penetration gets a firestop system listed for cable (priced with the alternative)
intents.risk: a cable firestop system must be listed for the assembly and the cable; the inspector checks each one

intents.reason: future capacity: the designed raceway is larger than its conductors need, so conductors can be added or replaced later
intents.risk: a cable can't take more conductors: a later upgrade means new cable, not a pull; if spare capacity is the intent, keep the raceway

intents.reason: physical protection: the runs are exposed where they can be damaged
intents.risk: a cable exposed to damage is not permitted (NEC 330.12(1), 334.15(B)); only raceway protects it

alternatives.name: Service-entrance cable (SER) for the feeders to the units' panels
alternatives.ampacity_why: NEC 338.10(B)(4)(a): SE cable used as an interior feeder under Part II of Article 334, in thermal insulation, is sized by the 60 °C column

code.says: Type SE cable may be used for interior wiring, feeders included, installed under Parts I and II of Article 334 (the NM rules, excluding 334.80); in thermal insulation its ampacity is the 60 °C column
NM-rule wiring is permitted in other structures permitted to be of Types III, IV and V construction, concealed behind a thermal barrier of at least a 15-minute finish rating
penetrations of fire-rated assemblies are firestopped to keep the rating

conditions: the building's construction type is III, IV or V (the code sheet's)
concealed in walls, floors and ceilings behind a 15-minute thermal barrier (gypsum board)
the conductors' ampacity checked at the 60 °C column where the cable is in thermal insulation
each rated penetration sealed with a firestop system listed for cable
the authority having jurisdiction confirms (local amendments may restrict cable wiring)

excluded_areas.exposed: NEC 334.15(B): exposed where subject to damage
excluded_areas.plenum: NEC 300.22(C): not in other spaces used for environmental air
excluded_areas.below_slab: NEC 334.12(B)(4) and 300.5: wet locations, in concrete and underground
excluded_areas.suspended: NEC 334.12(A)(2): not exposed within a dropped or suspended ceiling cavity of other than dwellings

alternatives.name: Nonmetallic-sheathed cable (NM) for the branch circuits concealed in the units
alternatives.ampacity_why: NEC 334.80: NM's ampacity is the 60 °C conductor rating's

code.says: NM is permitted in other structures permitted to be of Types III, IV and V construction, concealed within walls, floors or ceilings that give a thermal barrier of at least a 15-minute finish rating
NM is not permitted exposed within a dropped or suspended ceiling cavity in other than dwellings
60 °C ampacity; more than two cables bundled or through one sealed bored hole are adjusted under 310.15(C)(1)

conditions: the building's construction type is III, IV or V (the code sheet's)
concealed in walls, floors and ceilings behind a 15-minute thermal barrier (gypsum board)
each circuit's conductors checked at the 60 °C column and, where its homerun shares a bored hole, adjusted for bundling (334.80)
each rated penetration sealed with a firestop system listed for cable
the authority having jurisdiction confirms (the specification asks for it where it lists NM)

excluded_areas.common: outside the units (a separate alternative weighs the common areas)
excluded_areas.exposed: NEC 334.10(3): concealed only (334.15(B): exposed where subject to damage)
excluded_areas.suspended: NEC 334.12(A)(2): not exposed within a dropped or suspended ceiling cavity of other than dwellings
excluded_areas.plenum: NEC 300.22(C): not in other spaces used for environmental air
excluded_areas.below_slab: NEC 334.12(B)(4) and 300.5: wet locations, in concrete and underground

alternatives.name: Nonmetallic-sheathed cable (NM) for the branch circuits concealed in common areas under gypsum ceilings
alternatives.ampacity_why: NEC 334.80: NM's ampacity is the 60 °C conductor rating's

code.says: NM is permitted in other structures permitted to be of Types III, IV and V construction, concealed within walls, floors or ceilings that give a thermal barrier of at least a 15-minute finish rating
NM is not permitted exposed within a dropped or suspended ceiling cavity in other than dwellings
60 °C ampacity; more than two cables bundled or through one sealed bored hole are adjusted under 310.15(C)(1)

conditions: the building's construction type is III, IV or V (the code sheet's)
only where every room the circuit serves has a gypsum (not suspended) ceiling and no plenum
each circuit's conductors checked at the 60 °C column and adjusted for bundling (334.80)
the authority having jurisdiction confirms (the specification asks for it where it lists NM)

excluded_areas.unit: inside the units (a separate alternative weighs them)
excluded_areas.exposed: NEC 334.10(3): concealed only (334.15(B): exposed where subject to damage)
excluded_areas.suspended: NEC 334.12(A)(2): not exposed within a dropped or suspended ceiling cavity of other than dwellings
excluded_areas.plenum: NEC 300.22(C): not in other spaces used for environmental air
excluded_areas.rated_corridor: company default: a rated corridor's walls and ceiling membrane stay cable-free (each membrane penetration would need its own listed cable firestop; the AHJ may allow it)
excluded_areas.ceiling_unknown: this alternative is for documented gypsum ceilings only: the documents don't type these ceilings
excluded_areas.below_slab: NEC 334.12(B)(4) and 300.5: wet locations, in concrete and underground

alternatives.name: Metal-clad cable (MC) for the branch circuits concealed in walls and ceilings
alternatives.ampacity_why: NEC 330.80 and 110.14(C): the conductors' 90 °C rating derated, never above the terminations' 75 °C column

code.says: Type MC cable is permitted for branch circuits and feeders, concealed or exposed, in any construction type, including above suspended ceilings and in spaces used for environmental air (300.22(C)(1))
supported within 12 in of each box and at most every 6 ft
penetrations of fire-rated assemblies are firestopped to keep the rating

conditions: concealed, or exposed where not subject to physical damage (330.12(1))
each rated penetration sealed with a firestop system listed for the cable

excluded_areas.exposed: NEC 330.12(1): not where subject to physical damage
excluded_areas.below_slab: NEC 330.12(2) and 330.10(A)(11): not in concrete or underground unless identified for it

alternatives.name: Metal-clad cable (MC) for the exposed branch circuits
alternatives.ampacity_why: NEC 330.80 and 110.14(C): the conductors' 90 °C rating derated, never above the terminations' 75 °C column

code.says: Type MC cable is permitted exposed for branch circuits and feeders
Type MC cable is not permitted where subject to physical damage

conditions: exposed only where not subject to physical damage (330.12(1))

excluded_areas.below_slab: NEC 330.12(2): not in concrete or underground unless identified for it
